articles.title: Tim Cook made Apple unshakeable, now John Ternus has to shake it
articles.summary: Tech News News: There is an office at Apple's old Infinite Loop campus that has been locked and dark since 2011. It was Steve Jobs's, and when Tim Cook took over he n.
articles.body: There is an office at Apple's old Infinite Loop campus that has been locked and dark since 2011. It was Steve Jobs's, and when Tim Cook took over he never moved into it. Fifteen years later, nobody has.John Ternus is expected to take Cook's office at Apple Park. Cook kept his distance from the man he replaced and spent fifteen years being compared to him anyway. Ternus starts at Cook's desk, with Cook down the hall. He is staying on as executive chairman, has told colleagues he will keep running Washington and Beijing himself, and said as much in the note he sent staff on his last day in the job: he is not leaving Apple, he is stepping away from a role he loved.Every part of that is sensible. It also means the person who has spent fifteen years setting Apple's instincts is still there while the new man tries to change them.Cook's Apple was built to survive, not to surpriseConsider what he inherited in August 2011. Jobs had spent a decade making wagers that could have finished the company and kept winning them: the iMac, the iPod, a phone with no keyboard, a tablet nobody had asked for. That was the house style.Cook did something else. He looked at the iPhone, understood what it was worth, and spent fifteen years building a world around it so that leaving became unthinkable. The Watch in 2014, AirPods in 2016, then Apple Pay, Apple Music, iCloud and the App Store, each one charging a little every month. The services business he assembled out of that now earns more than all of Apple did on the day he started. Revenue roughly quadrupled to $416 billion, market value rose fifteenfold past $4.7 trillion, and there are now more than 2.5 billion active Apple devices in the world against a few hundred million when he arrived.None of it came from a product. It came from operations, which is what Cook had been doing since 1998. He knew what every component cost and where it came from, and he squeezed until the margins moved. Dropping Intel for Apple's own silicon took gross margins from about 40 per cent in 2011 to nearly 50 per cent today, which is the most consequential decision of his tenure and one you have never seen or been sold.He did swing occasionally, and it kept not landing. The Vision Pro was his, championed as the device that would make computing spatial and eventually succeed the phone, and it has ended up an expensive object for enthusiasts, with jobs now being cut across the programme. The iPhone Air was a new shape for the product that pays for everything and did not find its buyers. The car ran for a decade and several billion dollars before it was shut in 2024.What the operations work bought was a company that cannot be knocked over. Maps launched badly in 2012, he apologised in writing, the iPhone did not blink. Tariffs took $638 billion off Apple's value in three days last April and it came back within weeks. The EU took $14.4 billion in back taxes and about $4 billion more in fines, the US justice department sued over monopoly claims, App Store commissions were forced down in several markets and rival app stores prised open in Europe. Margins went up through all of it.That durability has a cost, and AI is where it showed up. Cook's method had never failed before: turn up late, turn up finished. Apple did not invent the MP3 player, the smartphone, the tablet, the smartwatch or wireless earbuds. It let someone else prove a category, then walked in with better hardware and better margins. AI did not wait. Apple Intelligence stumbled at launch in 2024, the Siri overhaul slipped by nearly two years, the acquisition Apple went shopping for never happened, and Cook removed the AI chief and reassigned the executive running Siri. Last year Apple gave up on its own models and started paying Google to put Gemini underneath Siri.Cook's memo describes the pattern without meaning to. The thing he says he is proudest of is what an annual report could never capture, that culture beats everything else. He is right, and it is the most revealing line in the letter. He built a culture, not a product, and cultures are magnificent at continuing to be themselves.Ternus builds things, which is the whole reason he has the jobHe is Apple's first chief executive in three decades to have spent his career on hardware, and that is the argument for him.He joined in 2001, after a mechanical engineering degree from Penn, where he swam varsity, and four years designing headsets at a virtual reality startup. His first work at Apple was on screens for Macs. By 2005 he was leading hardware engineering for the iMac G5, where his team wanted to hold the glass in place with magnets, an idea treated as odd at the time and one he pushed through anyway. Promoted to manager, he was offered an office and turned it down twice, staying in open seating with his team. He spent long stretches in Asia learning how hard it is to make a supplier deliver what a designer drew.His first note to staff was mostly thanks, which is what a first note to staff always is. What is interesting is where it ends. Not on the launch he calls phenomenal, but on what sits behind it, the products already in the works and the ones nobody has imagined yet. Cook's letters were about the team and the values. Ternus wrote his about the pipeline.Then there is the other Ternus. Around 2018, Apple weighed putting a small laser in the iPhone for better photos and mapping, at about $40 a device. Ternus, running hardware, proposed putting it only in the Pro models, on the reasoning that the loyalists would pay for new technology and nobody else would notice. Commercially it was the right call. It is also the reflex that kept Apple out of the AI race, and it now belongs to the chief executive. Six former employees have described him as better known for maintaining products than creating them. One former engineering manager put it more bluntly than anyone inside would like: if you want to make an iPhone every year, Ternus is your guy.He has been willing to say no to Cook's projects, though. He never accepted the Vision Pro argument, on the grounds that it was too heavy and too expensive to go mainstream, and Apple has been cutting that programme since he was elevated. He backs the smart glasses instead, and is said to be open to leaving head-worn devices altogether if they do not take.Cook is staying because Ternus needs him toStart with what he already has. The foldable iPhone next week, the first genuinely new shape the product has taken. A 20th anniversary iPhone in 2027. Then the things still some way off: smart glasses next year, AirPods with cameras that read your surroundings, a home display on a robotic arm, a wearable pendant, a touchscreen MacBook. All of it approved by Ternus as hardware chief, all of it the "already in the works" half of his memo, and more new hardware than Cook shipped in fifteen years. The other half, the products nobody has imagined yet, is the part that has to come from the new job.The difficulty is everything around the products. He is thin on finance, legal, procurement and government relations, which is most of a modern chief executive's week. Cook keeps Washington and Beijing, and has been personally working through the memory shortage that has already pushed up MacBook and iPad prices, with iPhones expected next. Analysts have started asking whether Apple's growth this year is coming from volume or from price.He also inherits a supply chain that exists in its current form only because an operations man built it. India assembles roughly a quarter of Apple's global iPhones now, about 55 million units in 2025, and the entire iPhone 17 line was made here before launch. Vietnam took AirPods, iPads and Watches. A small US assembly base was set up largely to satisfy Donald Trump, with a $600 billion investment pledge attached and promises of more. None of it was visionary. All of it was necessary, and it is now Ternus's to keep running while he tries to do something else.The bench is emptying at the same time. Jeff Williams, the chief operating officer long assumed to be the natural successor, retired in December after 27 years. Luca Maestri, finance chief for a decade, has moved into a smaller role. Phil Schiller gave up the App Store and Apple's product events days before the handover, which colleagues read as a step towards retiring outright, and he is the last visible link to the Jobs era. Roughly half the leadership team could be gone within a few years. Below them, engineers have been leaving for Meta and for OpenAI's hardware division, which Apple is now suing over trade secrets.So the pipeline says risk-taker and the record says careful, and Cook is still in the building.Next week will not tell you muchTernus stands on that stage next week while Cook sits in the room, off it for the first time in fifteen years. The wider Siri rollout lands the same week, which means his first month contains both the thing he built and the thing he inherited.The foldable will tell you nothing. A folding iPhone seven years after Samsung is what turning up late and finished looks like, and it would have shipped under Cook too. Watch for something duller: whether this company, under a product man, puts real money into something that does not pay for itself inside a product cycle, and whether a board that has enjoyed fifteen years without a bad quarter will sit through one while he tries.Signing out, Cook wrote that Apple made its dent in the universe because of what it values and how it sees the world. That culture is the most valuable thing he built and the hardest thing about the job he has handed over. It survived every blow the last fifteen years threw at it, and it is the reason Apple was two years late to the only technology that has mattered since the iPhone. Ternus does not have to dismantle it. He has to prove it can still be surprised.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Apple follows Google Maps, renames Lake Ontario to Lake America; US President calls change of names 'complete, ratified, and binding'
articles.summary: Tech News News: After Google Maps, Apple Maps has now renamed Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for users in the US after a presidential executive order. The update mean.
articles.body: After Google Maps, Apple Maps has now renamed Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for users in the US after a presidential executive order. The update means Apple users in the United States will see ‘Lake America’ when viewing the Great Lake that sits between New York and Canada’s Ontario province. Users outside the US will continue to see the lake as Lake Ontario. Sharing a post on X (formerly Twitter), US President Donald Trump called the name change 'complete, ratified, and binding'.“Apple Maps has just announced that it has changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, so now that very important change of names, between Google Maps and Apple Maps, is complete, ratified, and binding. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP,” Trump wrote in the post.Apple follows Google Maps with Lake America changeGoogle Maps changed its display label for Lake Ontario over the weekend, saying it was following the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), which had formally changed the name in the United States. Google then said its Maps service would show different names depending on the user’s location. People in the US would see “Lake America”, users in Canada would see “Lake Ontario”, while users outside the US and Canada would see both names.Canada continues to call it Lake OntarioCanadian officials have rejected the name change and said the country will continue using Lake Ontario in its official records. Prime Minister Mark Carney has pointed to the history of the name, saying it is more than 400 years old and comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io.“The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America,” Carney said.MapQuest refuses to rename the lakeNotably, not every mapping service has followed Google and Apple. MapQuest has rejected the request to use “Lake America”. The company posted a screenshot showing the name Lake Ontario with the message: “We’re not changing it.” According to a Guardian report, the move reportedly helped MapQuest rise to the top of Apple’s US App Store rankings.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: TMC alleges 'systematic misuse of police' by BJP in Bengal; writes to President Murmu
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) on Thursday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu and West Bengal governor RN Ravi, seeking time for party delegat.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) on Thursday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu and West Bengal governor RN Ravi, seeking time for party delegations to meet them and highlight the alleged lawlessness in the state.The TMC accused the ruling BJP of “systematically misusing” the West Bengal Police, calling it “disturbing.”"TMC workers are being targeted by the police across the state. Party offices are being vandalised. The police are following no rules. Police are acting openly as BJP cadres. There is utter lawlessness here. In this situation, we have written to the President of India, and the Trinamool Congress has written to the Governor of West Bengal, seeking an urgent appointment of a Trinamool Congress delegation to discuss the disturbing situation in Bengal," the party's Rajya Sabha MP Derek O'Brien told reporters.The development came hours after TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that "BJP hooligans armed with weapons" stormed the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata in the early hours of the day and vandalised the premises, assaulted staff, and damaged electronic equipment."What happened at Camac Street this morning is a disgraceful assault on the rule of law. At around 4.30 am, BJP hooligans, armed with weapons, stormed our party office in the heart of Kolkata. They attacked our people, snatched their phones, smashed furniture, ransacked the premises and destroyed electronic equipment. And where was Kolkata Police? For nearly TWO HOURS, despite repeated calls and emails from our people and lawyers, there was no response. This is outrageous and unacceptable. We demand the immediate arrest of every person involved in this attack," he wrote on X.The Diamond Harbour MP, nephew of TMC supremo and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, asked chief minister Suvendu Adhikari if he was “scared” of the TMC and was therefore resorting to "intimidation."“This is what the BJP has done to my party office in the early hours of this morning. Will the Governor of WB act? Will the Union Home Minister act? Will the PMO act? Or will they continue to look the other way? It is high time the judiciary, particularly the Calcutta High Court, takes serious note of what is happening and acts to uphold the rule of law in West Bengal. And one simple question for Suvendu Adhikari: why are you so scared of the Trinamool Congress and of me that you have to resort to this kind of intimidation? If this is how the Opposition is to be treated in West Bengal, through violence, vandalism and intimidation, then the Chief Minister has no moral authority to remain in office. He must resign. This is not democracy. This is political thuggery... Nothing will be forgotten,” Abhishek Banerjee added.The BJP, meanwhile, rejected Abhishek Banerjee’s allegation of “vendetta”, arguing that if that were the case, no TMC leader would have remained “unscathed” after the party’s defeat in the April assembly elections, which ended its 15-year rule in West Bengal."If the BJP were engaging in vendetta politics, then after the election results were declared, none of the defeated Trinamool Congress MLAs, ministers, and MPs would have remained unscathed... Trinamool members are throwing eggs at each other and vandalising each other's offices. Those who faced injustice at the hands of Abhishek Banerjee, when he was a top party leader, understand the situation," BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: PM Modi photo removal row: BJP panel leaves KDMC Mahayuti exit decision to Ravindra Chavan
articles.summary: KALYAN: The political row over the removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s photograph at a college in Pune by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) worke.
articles.body: KALYAN: The political row over the removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s photograph at a college in Pune by Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers has now spilled into the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC), with the BJP’s local leadership leaving the final decision on whether to quit the Mahayuti alliance in the civic body to state BJP president Ravindra Chavan.The BJP’s core committee held a meeting in Kalyan on Wednesday against the backdrop of the party’s warning that it would withdraw from the alliance and sit in the Opposition if Shiv Sena (Shinde) failed to sever its alliance with the MNS and remove the party from power in the civic body.BJP deputy mayor Rahul Damle said the core committee had taken an important decision and forwarded it to Chavan for a final call. He, however, declined to disclose the details.The development follows a letter issued by BJP district president Nandu Parab on Tuesday to Shiv Sena Kalyan district chief Gopal Landge, demanding action against the MNS. The Shinde Sena has so far not officially responded to the letter.However, Shiv Sena deputy district chief Rajesh Kadam hit back at the BJP, saying the party should not lecture the Sena on coalition dharma. He pointed to the BJP’s conduct in Ambernath and Bhiwandi and questioned whether the BJP had itself followed alliance principles in those areas.The issue has also put the local alliance partners in a delicate position. Kalyan MP and Shiv Sena leader Dr Shrikant Shinde has not publicly commented on the BJP’s warning, while MNS leader Raju Patil has also maintained silence on the demand.The MNS had earlier indicated that its local-level response to the controversy was an internal matter.The BJP core committee meeting was attended by senior party leader Jagannath Patil, MLA Sulabha Gaikwad and BJP corporators, among others.While none of the committee members disclosed the decision, sources said the panel favoured asking the Shinde Sena to remove the MNS from the civic administration.The BJP is understood to have also considered sitting in the Opposition if the Sena refuses to act against the MNS. However, party leaders are now awaiting Chavan’s decision before taking any further step.The immediate question is whether the state BJP president will endorse the core committee’s decision and formally direct the local unit to withdraw from the Mahayuti arrangement in KDMC. The decision could have a direct bearing on the balance of power in the civic body.Meanwhile, Congress group leader in the KDMC took a swipe at the BJP over the ongoing alliance row, alleging that the party was merely indulging in political posturing.“The BJP is only staging a political stunt. It cannot stay away from power, and the current talk of sitting in the Opposition is nothing but a show,” she said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Thane | Silver Rate in Thane | Bank Holidays in Thane | Public Holidays in Thane | Petrol Price in Thane | Diesel Price in Thane | CNG Price in Thane | LPG Price in ThaneStay updated with the latest Thane news. articles.title: Too many allies? Why Netanyahu's far-right partners are hurting him in upcoming Israel polls
articles.summary: Middle East News: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing an unusual threat ahead of the October 27 election: divisions within the far-right bloc that suppo.
articles.body: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing an unusual threat ahead of the October 27 election: divisions within the far-right bloc that support his government.Smotrich’s Religious Zionism and Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power, which ran together in the 2022 elections, have rejected Netanyahu's calls for another merger amid tensions. Meanwhile, smaller parties led by former Likud members and former general Ofer Winter are competing for the same right-wing voters, deepening fragmentation.“When we unite, we win. When we split up, we lose,” Netanyahu told Israel's local media outlet Channel 14, according to AP.Netanyahu currently heads a coalition of religious and ultranationalist parties.Netanyahu’s Likud party on Friday rebuked national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for refusing to run on a joint slate with finance minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism party, warning that a divided vote could weaken the coalition’s chances of retaining power.Several smaller parties are competing for the same right-wing electorate, raising the prospect that some could fall below Israel’s electoral threshold and leave their votes without parliamentary representation.Under Israel’s electoral system, parties must secure at least 3.25 per cent of the vote to win representation in the 120-member Knesset. A party that falls below the threshold receives no seats, making fragmentation particularly consequential for Netanyahu’s bloc.The Financial Times reported that Netanyahu has sparred publicly with Ben-Gvir, who rejected a meeting this week to discuss a merger with Smotrich. Ben-Gvir accused the prime minister of an “attempt to weaken” his Jewish Power party.Netanyahu responded by urging Ben-Gvir to “not burn tens of thousands of rightwing votes . . . and crown a leftwing government”, while also telling him to “overcome your personal ego”.Ben-Gvir, however, argues that a merger could cost his party seats. “According to all the polls, a connection between me and Smotrich distances Jewish Strength by 3-4 mandates who won't come to vote, and the right-wing government will fall!” he wrote on X.The dispute has left Netanyahu pressing harder for unity. In a video posted on X, he said Smotrich and Ben-Gvir “must unite. Every time we ran united, we won. When we ran separately, we lost.”“In 1992, the Right had more votes than the Left, like today, but because we were running separately, we got the disaster of Oslo, Arafat, Hamas and recurring catastrophes,” Netanyahu said, referring to the peace process launched through the Oslo Accords.Smotrich appeared more receptive, writing on X, “It's time for unity and responsibility in the national camp.”Netanyahu subsequently invited Ben-Gvir and Smotrich to meet on Sunday, saying, “We must not waste a single vote; we must unite to save the right-wing bloc!”The stakes are high for Netanyahu, whose nearly uninterrupted 17 years in power are being tested in an election shaped by the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, mass protests and wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.The parties have until September 8 to decide whether to merge, withdraw or contest the election separately.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'In any manner': EAM Jaishankar says India ready to help end Russia-Ukraine war
articles.summary: India News: External affairs minister S Jaishankar speaking in Kyiv said that India is ready to contribute to efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war “in any manner.
articles.body: External affairs minister S Jaishankar speaking in Kyiv said that India is ready to contribute to efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war “in any manner” possible.“If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there,” Jaishankar said, as quoted by news agency Reuters.Jaishankar is on a three-day visit to Ukraine and Poland from September 3 to 5, his first visit to Kyiv since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. During the visit, he is holding bilateral consultations with Sybiha as well as Polish Deputy Prime Minister Radoslaw Sikorski.Jaishankar’s remarks come days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi renewed his call for an end to the conflict during a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.“Every day spent in the war pushes humanity back. And every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm. We will have to move from an endless war to an end of war, which is very important for humanity's well-being,” PM Modi said.He added: “That all issues are resolved peacefully as soon as possible is the call of humanity. This is the message of India. This is the message of the land of Gandhi and the land of Buddha - the path to peace.”PM Modi has repeatedly called for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict. In 2022, he told Putin that “this is not the era of war”, while during his 2024 visit to Moscow, he said that no solution could be found on the battlefield.Jaishankar’s Kyiv visit comes amid heightened hostilities and concerns in New Delhi after an Indian was killed in the Ukrainian capital this week following a Russian strike. India has also raised concerns over attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Full-time nagging women": Candace Owens delivers fiery reality check to men amid growing Lindsay Clancy debate
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Candace Owens has turned the focus of the Lindsay Clancy debate toward an unexpected target: men online. In a pointed discussion, Owens argued that so.
articles.body: Candace Owens has turned the focus of the Lindsay Clancy debate toward an unexpected target: men online. In a pointed discussion, Owens argued that social media has created a culture where some men spend their days criticizing women, chasing extreme examples and turning every viral controversy into another complaint. Her remarks come as debate over Clancy supporters continues to spread across platforms such as TikTok and X.Candace Owens takes aim at men’s online behaviorOwens’ argument is less about defending every reaction to the Lindsay Clancy case and more about questioning how internet users build sweeping conclusions from isolated posts.She pushed back against what she described as a growing habit of finding the most outrageous example of a woman’s behavior online and using it to make claims about women as a whole. In her view, that approach strips away context and turns complicated issues into easy arguments designed for social media engagement.But Owens also believes the criticism has created an unexpected reversal. Instead of women being portrayed as the problem, she suggested that some men have become consumed by constant online complaints.She explained:"There is currently a fleet of men on X who have been making the argument that women need to get off of TikTok, right? They cite, there's this game of citing, finding extreme examples, of course, of not the average woman doing and saying absurd things, like you've seen some of these TikToks in support of Lindsay Clancy. This has become very fashionable, by the way, avoiding nuance, finding an extreme example, and then being like, this proves my point that all women are insane."She adde, "I'd like to make the counter argument that the internet is currently turning a lot of men into full-time nagging women. They're just online lodging complaints 24-7 a day, 24-7 about issues that they don't even necessarily care about, they don't even necessarily know about. They're just here to complain, complain, complain. And this is now really bothering me about the podcast space. Not everybody needs to have a podcast, least of all men who just want to log on and complain every day. Did you hear what Tucker said? Did you hear what Candace said? Did you hear what Tucker and Candace said? We just don't need it."Lindsay Clancy debate sparks wider conversationThe remarks highlight a larger problem with online discourse: outrage can travel much faster than context.The Lindsay Clancy case has generated intense reactions, and social media has given users a place to express sympathy, anger and competing interpretations. Yet Owens argues that focusing on extreme posts can distort the broader conversation. A viral TikTok may attract thousands of views precisely because it is unusual, not because it represents the average person.That distinction matters. Social media rewards content that provokes a strong response, while quieter and more measured opinions rarely receive the same attention.Owens also turned her criticism toward the expanding podcast culture, where personalities can build entire discussions around what another commentator said hours earlier. Her frustration was clear: endless commentary can become a cycle in which people react to reactions rather than engage with the original issue.Her comments are likely to fuel another round of debate, particularly among users already divided over the Lindsay Clancy discussion. But her central point goes beyond one case. She is challenging the habit of treating the loudest voices online as representative of everyone, while warning that constant digital outrage can consume both men and women.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Wai Wai bhujia under FSSAI scanner: Ajmer firm told to stop production, 32,000kg stock seized
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Food regulator FSSAI on Thursday said it has directed CG Foods India Pvt Ltd to stop production of 'Veg Bhujia Namkeen' after inspections foun.
articles.body: JAIPUR: Food regulator FSSAI on Thursday said it has directed CG Foods India Pvt Ltd to stop production of 'Veg Bhujia Namkeen' after inspections found multiple violations, including hygiene-related lapses.The food safety and standards authority of india (FSSAI) said it had initiated enforcement action against CG Foods India in view of "unsafe processing, unlicensed bhujia manufacturing, and predated packaging".FSSAI conducted an inspection at the company's unit in Roopangarh, Ajmer, Rajasthan, to check manufacturing practices and hygiene compliance, news agency PTI reported."The unit was found re-processing floor-collected, broken noodles into bhujia products without heat treatment, along with using predated packaging dates. Unlicensed manufacturing of 'Wai-Wai MaMa' and 'Wai-Wai Mama Punte' bhujia variants was identified in direct violation of Section 31(1) of the FSS Act, 2006," FSSAI said.The regulator seized 32,107.2 kg of stock at the premises, including loose broken noodles."The inspection revealed several hygiene and documentation deficiencies, including inadequate pest-control records and other deficiencies relating to food hygiene and safety," FSSAI said.Samples were collected for laboratory analysis, while 1,925 boxes of expired finished goods were detained, PTI reported.FSSAI also initiated strict legal proceedings against the company.The regulator directed the company to "discontinue the production of the Veg Bhujia Namkeen products without proper approvals and measures".FSSAI warned that further regulatory action would follow based on the laboratory analysis and inspection findings.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news.
